replaced_entry.divergence: The secondary2002 petition inserts Filii immediately after Christi before tui; substitutes da for dona; inserts hominis after terreni. These are explicit small grammatical/relationship clarifications of the same old petition, not silently declared orthography. The secondary2002 omits the ancient closing Christi Domini nostri. Qui tecum vivit, and supplies the common short conclusion Per Christum Dominum nostrum. with a separately marked R. Amen. The complete short formula and marked response are independently image-witnessed in old Lasance at artifact217/printed217. haereditariam/hereditariam is spelling; stress accents, capitalization and pointing differ. Ancient footnote markers8–10 are apparatus, not wording. No modern fullbody is retained in this proposal. The complete finite relationship, including all three small clarifications and common conclusion change, requires independent source and rights review before admission; no exact whole-word target fidelity or authenticated2008 reading is claimed. Study English only. Independently witnessed ancient petition with enumerated omission/grammatical variants and independently witnessed generic conclusion; not approved current liturgical English, not authenticated2008 correspondence, not an instruction for recitation. translations.text:
O God, who through the Passion of Christ your Son, our Lord, have undone the death inherited from ancient sin, into which the whole human race had fallen, grant that, made like him, as we have borne the image of the earthly man by the necessity of nature, so we may bear the image of the heavenly one through sanctification by grace. Through Christ our Lord.
R. Amen.
